title: Known-public key record: the Hardhat default account #0 private key (six fork files) and account #1 (honeypotMultiAmount) are committed as fork-only signers; they are public test keys, not a leak, and are recorded without escalation

evidence.note: FORK_ONLY_TEST_KEY = Hardhat account #0 (shared by captureRehearsal, deliberateBuyReplay, exitStatePersistence, realLaunchReplay)
asserts the constant equals the Hardhat #0 key

evidence.ref: grep -rnoE "0x[0-9a-fA-F]{64}" over the TESTI snapshot (excluding fork fixtures, which hold tx hashes)
evidence.note: the only 32-byte hex literals in the slice are these two Hardhat keys and two synthetic receipt.fixtures values (0xabcdef...7890, 0xdeadbeef...); no other key-shaped value

sibling_sites_checked: Every file of the slice grepped for key-shaped literals and key words (PRIVATE_KEY, privateKey, Wallet(, mnemonic, 0x + 64 hex): integration files use "0x" + "1"x64 (wsReconnect:38) and "0x" + "1"x64 auth keys (txManager, mevStrategies), synthetic; api.fixtures MOCK_API_KEY is synthetic; no fixture or README holds a credential value (realLaunches/README.md:45-49 describes which env var holds the operator's archive key without its value).
severity_rationale: S4 record: Hardhat #0 and #1 are published development keys (PROTOCOL section 4 and D-17: known-public, never escalated).
recommendation: None required for safety. Phase 28 may centralise the two keys in the realMainnetGate helper so scanners have one known-public location to allow-list.
